title: By the Rivers of Babylon
program_note: By the Rivers of Babylon is a setting of the first line of Psalm 137, based upon a 16th-century (or earlier) Russian Orthodox chant in an old Russian dialect.  It was commissioned by the international music competition St. Petersburg in the Mirror of the World’s Cultural Heritage, as the required contemporary composition for the piano accompaniment competition.  In contrast to the restrained vocal line, the piano part is meant to bring out the emotional content of the text, with in-the-piano techniques used to evoke anguished sobs and falling tears.   It is the first of the Two Russian Psalm Settings.
